$comment: Shared corpus for the pipeline-health OVERALL score (#1197). Two implementations answer 'what is the health score' for the same dimension results: the SDK engine (packages/nightgauge-sdk/src/analysis/health/HealthAnalysisEngine.ts, computeOverallHealthScore) and this skill's Phase 3 rule. Both are pinned to every case below by packages/nightgauge-sdk/tests/analysis/health/overallScore.corpusParity.test.ts, so a change to either has to change this file too. The rule: a dimension without enough data is EXCLUDED and the surviving weights are re-normalised; overall = round(sum(score * weight) / sum(weight)) over the dimensions that have data, clamped to [0, 100]; null (rendered N/A) when no dimension has data. A no-data dimension's placeholder score is never read.

cases.rationale: Baseline: every dimension counts at its table weight.
The bug in #1197: model-routing with no data used to contribute 0.12 x 50 forever. Excluding it and re-normalising leaves the overall equal to the surviving dimensions' weighted mean.
Whatever number a starved analyzer leaves in `score` (50, 0, 100) must not move the overall.
Weights do not need to sum to 1; the divisor is the sum over dimensions with data (0.3), not the table total (0.5).
Absence of evidence is N/A, not 0 (critical) and not 50 (fair).
A --dimensions filter that selects nothing has nothing to score.
A dimension weighted 0 has data but no vote; if it is the only one with data there is still no score.
